title: Enawene Nawe - Wikipedia
text: The Enawenê-Nawê are an Indigenous people of Brazil in the Mato Grosso state. They live in a large village near the Iquê River in the Enawenê Nawê Indigenous Land. [1] They practice agriculture, fishing, and gathering and do not hunt or eat red meat. The Enawene Nawe are a relatively isolated people who were first contacted in 1974 by Vicente Cañas.
